title: Chris Kelly's band and George Popper
summary: Playing with Chris Kelly, who paid well, and the pianist and trombone man George Popper.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Chris Kelly, the blues trumpeter and his band

blocks.x: Well, that about brings us up to date on the brass bands, I think. Huh? We know pretty much what's happened since then. So I got a reference to that, I've written down. Now, did you play with many other dance bands other than your own? Oh, yeah, I think. You know Chris Kelly? I heard of him. Chris Kelly, like, got some money. He said, guys, they're triple the money. Can't keep nobody.
How's the bond? You play a trombone. Mm-hm. money can't keep nobody. How's the bondage of their tram? You know the fat out of it, good tram. We talk good tram.
And who else was in the band? Have a piano player or not?
They used piano players, Sam? Piano player? Mm-hmm. I'd use piano players sometime.
No, I mean Chris Kelly, did he use it?
He would sometime? Yeah, George E. Popper used to play with him.
He thought about that and all that.
That happened to me. I saw George E. Popper the other day.
George E. Popper died, didn't he?
No. I saw him at Eddie Pearson's Wake.
Yeah? He's crippled, man. He crippled? He saw a brosket.
